name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateAttachTransform
summary: Per-frame update of a field actor's attach/effect state: when +0x29C is set it calls Model_Attach_SetFadeRange on the handle at +0x160, copies the position/rotation words at +0x260..+0x278 into the visible-transform fields (+0x9C..+0xA4 and +0xC0..+0xC8), rebuilds a direction vector from the four rotation components and hands it to Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, then parks the weapon animation at time 0.
evidence: Callees are now named (Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection, Model_Attach_SetFadeRange, 0x003E8BF0 Field actor helper) and the body matches that sequence, but the only caller is itself an unproven maybe_ name and nothing in the body identifies which object is attached, so the 'attach' wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateWeaponAttachRange
signature: int maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateWeaponAttachRange(FieldActor* self, int arg2, int arg3, int *owner)
summary: Per-frame weapon-attach watchdog: when the UI overlay byte (work+8->+0x48, +0x284) is clear it compares the weapon position (+0x27/+0x29) with the body position (+0x30/+0x32) and drops the attachment once the distance exceeds the epsilon 0x34000000 (Model_Attach_SetFadeRange on +0x160, clears +0xA7 and sets +0xA8 to -1); in the scripted-pose branch it counts the hold time at +0xA8 down and calls vtable +0x98 when it reaches zero. Always returns 1.
evidence: The readable body matches the disassembly (float distance compare against 0x34000000 and the +0xA8 countdown), but there is still no caller and the vtable +0x98 callback is unnamed, so the class and the 'attach' role remain inferred.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Release
summary: Teardown half of a scene-object pair: if the handle at +0x384 (self+900) is valid it queries 0x005F708C and clears the fade range; then it destroys the object found through 0x003F422C(self+0x370) via its vtable slot +0x88 and finally releases the object with 0x005F58BC.
evidence: Its twin 0x00181C14 (slot +0x84 then 0x005F6000) is unchanged and both are still reached only through tables, so 'Release' is the reading of the +0x88 teardown slot, not a named engine concept.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyParam
summary: Value-applying half of the same scene-object pair: same handle/fade prefix, then, when the object found through 0x003F422C(self+0x370) exists and its +0x51 byte is clear, calls its vtable slot +0x84 with the value and forwards the value to 0x005F6000(self, value).
evidence: The pairing with 0x0018193C is byte-for-byte in the prefix and both tail calls are unnamed mid-function symbols; what the value means is still unknown, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_BattleActor_ShowStateEffect
summary: Battle-actor effect/state display: fills the request record at self+0xB0 (type 6, count 1, id 6, effect id from +0xB2 or 0x13), builds the transform/anchor record, marks the anchor at +0x48 as mode 7 and calls Battle_Unit_UpdateEffectAnchors; then touches the bag/save block (work+0x24A98), updates the actor's sound handle and sets state 0x10.
evidence: Caller Battle_SetActorEffectId and the callees (Battle_Unit_UpdateEffectAnchors, the Gfx/Ui transform helpers, the sound refresh) all fit a 'show state effect' step, but the item/bag call at 0x00614024 and the effect-id source are still unexplained, so the exact verb stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_StopActionAnim
summary: Finishes the owning field actor's current action: when the actor (component-0x22C) is visible it plays animation 0x002F2F08 in mode 0, snaps the animator to the last frame, sets vtable state 4 and clears the component's +0x5C and +0xAC counters.
evidence: The body shows no effect attach or detach at all - only an animation play, a jump to last frame and state 4 - so the previous 'StopAttachedEffect' wording asserted something the code does not do; the actor class is still inferred from the -0x22C back-pointer and the animation helper, hence maybe_.

name: Field_Object_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field object: it unlinks the two intrusive list nodes at +0x22C/+0x24C, destroys the member at +0x24C (0x0017C330), runs the Field base destructor (0x00335DAC Field_Object_DtorBase) and tail-calls the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The readable C attached to this address is stale (it shows a one-line wrapper around 0x005F4F5C); the disassembly is unambiguous: push {r4,lr}; str r1,[r0],#0x22c; str r2,[r0],#0x20; ldm/str list unlink; bl 0x0017C330; bl 0x00335DAC (Field_Object_DtorBase); pop; b 0x0010F6CC (the shared free thunk, see R3_022). That is a deleting destructor, not an animation stop.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_HandleCount
summary: Item-screen quantity step: requires the page scroll to be finished, resolves the member record for the selected party slot (u8 +0x10 < 0x1F) with 0x0035EB98, compares the current quantity (+0xC) with the member's owned count (0x006293A8) to decide whether the +/- step is legal, updates the number pane and returns the next handler pair from 0x00729554.
evidence: The disassembly confirms the member-slot bound 0x1F, the signed direction field +0x14, the quantity field +0xC and the owned-count compare, so 'HandleCount' describes the body; it is kept maybe_ because the C is truncated by bad instruction data and there is no direct caller (vtable/table slot only).

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_BeginSelect
summary: Item-screen step handler: if the page scroll is finished it chains to maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_ShowSelectionResult with the context flags cleared; otherwise it writes screen command 10, reactivates the screen and returns the default handler pair from the 0x00729554 table (+4/+8).
evidence: Same skeleton as the sibling slots and it calls the still-unproven ShowSelectionResult; no direct caller, so the 'BeginSelect' verb cannot be separated from the other step handlers.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntry
summary: Item-screen step handler: when the page scroll is finished it chains to maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx with the confirm flag 0x10100 set; otherwise it returns the default handler pair from 0x00729554 (+0x24/+0x28).
evidence: The 0x10100 flag marks the positive/confirm path of this family (0x001BFB64 and 0x001C0A24 clear it), which supports 'SelectEntry'; still table-only and there is no direct caller.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_Cancel
summary: Item-screen step handler for the cancel path: if the page scroll is not finished it returns the default handler pair (0x00729554+0x24/+0x28); otherwise it tears down the lists (maybe_Ui_MainMenu_TeardownLists), notifies the screen's vtable +0x5C when +0x22E0 is clear and returns the second pair (0x00729554+0x34/+0x38).
evidence: The cleared-context branch plus the teardown calls support the cancel/back reading, but the specific verb (Cancel vs Back) is still inferred and there is no direct caller.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_SelectEntryEx(UiItemScreen* item, int screen, char* flags)
summary: Main item-screen entry action: if the selected list index is past 0x1E it buys the item for the member (maybe_Shop_BuyItemForMember) and jumps to command 0xB/0x17; otherwise it looks the item up, rejects equipment already worn by the member, checks the owned count and branches to commands 0xC/0xD before returning the matching handler pair from 0x00729554.
evidence: All four callers are item-screen handlers (SelectEntry, HandleCursorInput, MoveCursor and 0x001BF8DC) and the callees are Item_LookupRecord plus the shop/party helpers; the individual command ids remain unnamed, which is why the generic 'SelectEntryEx' wording is kept.

name: maybe_Ui_State_SetState2
summary: Initialises a six-word transition record with the 0xFF/0xFFFF invalid defaults, notifies the active screen through its manager vtable +0x5C, sets screen command 2 and copies the two-word handler target from 0x00729554+4/+8 into the record.
evidence: Callers (Ui_Window_RegisterEventContextB, Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor, 0x001C10CC) tie it to the shop/item window state machine, but 'SetState2' just restates the command constant 2 and the record's owner is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_State_HandleEvent
summary: One step of a window state machine: pulls the current input event (0x00641F7C) and forwards its x/y/z to the child at screen+0x184 through vtable +0x3C; on event bit 0x102 it calls 0x00311018 and picks the step-1 (maybe_Ui_State_SetState2), step-2 (maybe_Ui_State_SetState24) or step-0x18 helper and stores the next handler pair from 0x007297BC.
evidence: The vtable constant 0x007297BC is shared with the named Ui_Window_OnActiveStateChanged / Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor code, which fixes 'window state machine'; the step meanings are still unknown, so HandleEvent stays generic.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_UpdateTransitionState
summary: Drives a window's open/close transition: if the screen state at +0x1E18 is 1 it copies the descriptor rectangle, scrolls the message window by -f_3C*f_1C0, sets animation state 7 and notifies the slot control; otherwise it copies the other descriptor pair, sets state 4 and notifies the same control.
evidence: The 4/7 state choice and the named Ui_Screen_UpdateTransition helper (0x00444E20) support the transition reading, but one branch also scrolls text through the message window, so which window class owns this slot is still open.

name: maybe_Ui_State_Reset
summary: Clears a 0x20-byte state block at +4 after releasing the reference at +0x2C when it was live, zeroes +0x24, and returns the word that was at +4 (the previous state id).
evidence: The memset/release sequence is clear and matches the sibling state-machine records, but there is no caller and the record's owner is unnamed; 'Reset' is still the only safe verb.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_UpdateChildren
summary: Per-frame update of a menu window: runs the window's own vtable +0x2C update, updates the list at +0x138 and the helper at 0x0018FCF0, then optionally forwards the pending input event to the child pane at +0x1E80 (when its flag bit 0 is set) and updates the pane at +0x1E34 (+0x1E48).
evidence: The two optional children are individual fields rather than a list and their flags are unnamed, so 'UpdateChildren' only describes the call pattern.

name: Gfx_EntryPool_Init
signature: void Gfx_EntryPool_Init(void* self, uint32_t owner, uint32_t owner2)
summary: Initialises a gfx scene entry pool: stores the heap tag at +8, allocates the two 8-byte allocator wrappers at +0xC/+0x10, a 0x14-byte occupancy header at +0x18 and 16 entries of 0x34 bytes plus a sentinel, then hands every entry to Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry and clears the occupancy bitmask.
evidence: The sibling Gfx_EntryPool_Clear (0x002E6428, caller Field_DestroyScene) frees exactly these 16 x 0x34 entries through the +0x18 occupancy bitmask, and all three callers here are field-scene code (Field_InitSceneObjects, Field_QueryOccludersInBoxLayer, maybe_Field_QuerySceneRect). The old 'Battle_PopupPool' prefix came only from the shared allocator-wrapper vtable, which 0x00627404 also installs in a field handle list.

name: Math_Random_InitState
signature: void Math_Random_InitState(RandomState* rng, uint32_t key0, uint32_t key1)
summary: Seeds a 6-word random state: calls 0x00113590 to build {key0, key1, 0x6C078965, 0x5D588B65, 0x00269EC3, 0} on the stack and stores that block at rng+8. The two constants 0x6C078965 and 0x5D588B65 are the MT19937 initialisation multipliers.
evidence: The sole call site is Field_InitSceneObjects calling it on &battleWork->f_4218, and FACTS.md places the battle RNG at battle work+0x4218 with 0x001CA474(rng,lo,hi) rolling from it; the three literal-pool words at 0x001135C0 are 0x6C078965/0x5D588B65/0x00269EC3 (RNG init multipliers). So the six copied words are an RNG state, not a colour.

name: maybe_Field_CreateStateObject
summary: Initialises a 0x124-byte field state object in place: installs vtable 0x0075A444, clears the state bytes, zero-fills the 0x12-byte counter block at +3 and sets its first byte to 1.
evidence: Callers are Field_InitSceneObjects and Battle_Encounter_BuildConditions, i.e. two different owners, and the body only stores a vtable and clears counters, so 'StateObject' is still a label for 'the object this vtable introduces'.

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_OpenSession
signature: unsigned int maybe_Svc_AcClient_OpenSession(Connection* conn, unsigned int* errorOut, unsigned int* reasonOut)
summary: Open/re-check of a service session: on the first call it validates or creates the handle at conn+0x18 (svcCloseHandle 0x23 for a stale one, 0x0012038C to create), queries the 512-byte state through 0x0050175C and sends it with 0x005016CC; success sets conn+0x9C54 and returns 1, otherwise it stores the nn::Result in errorOut/reasonOut.
evidence: The callees are now named as ac:u session helpers (Svc_AcClient_CheckSession, maybe_Svc_AcClient_GetAccountState) and the handle lifecycle uses svc 0x23/0x24 (FACTS.md), but both callers are the Fs file-job state machines (Fs_FileJob_Update/UpdateAlt), which does not fit an account session - so the subsystem is not settled.

name: maybe_Field_ApplyToActorsInRadius
signature: void maybe_Field_ApplyToActorsInRadius(FieldWork* scene, float* position, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actor list (work+8->+0x54, class list 4) and for every actor within the squared radius of the position (and, when filter is 0, not in state 2) calls 0x005E7848(actor,2,0) and the actor's virtual +0x98; called from the slide-window play-in/play-out paths.
evidence: The radius walk and the fixed operation are unchanged; 0x005E7848 is still unnamed, so 'ApplyToActorsInRadius' deliberately stays vague, and the only callers are themselves maybe_ slide-window names.

name: maybe_Field_DetachActorsInRadius
signature: void maybe_Field_DetachActorsInRadius(ViewWork* self, float* position, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actors around a position and detaches the matching ones: asks Field_AttachSlotObject for the actor's slot and, when that succeeds, decrements the view-entry counters +0x15E0/+0x15E4 (state-2 actors use +0x15E4), then clamps the entry height; called from the talk-camera release path.
evidence: Field_AttachSlotObject and Field_TalkCamera_ReleaseWork are now named, which supports 'detach actors in radius'; the ViewWork class and the counter fields are still inferred.

name: maybe_ViewWork_AddRowsFromBuffer
signature: void maybe_ViewWork_AddRowsFromBuffer(ViewList* list, ListHead* head, uint32_t alloc)
summary: Copies up to 0x20 row descriptors from the embedded 0x1C-stride buffer at list+0x100 into fresh 0x18-byte list nodes (skipping the 0x0FFFFFFF empty rows) and appends each to the given list head.
evidence: Callers Field_TalkCamera_ReleaseWork and Gfx_MeshObject_ApplySetupParams fix the two lists but not the class; the body is a generic row copy with unnamed helpers, so the ViewWork wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Text_ConstructRowTable
summary: Builds a 4x6 array of 0x5F9720-type elements on the stack and, when the alternate flag is 0, also reads the game work and a save-work byte table (work+0x24A98). The decompiled body ends in the array constructor, so the consumer is not visible.
evidence: Called only by Text_LayoutSingleLine, but the body contains no string handling - it is one std_ConstructArray(dst, 0x005F9720, 4, 6) plus a save-work lookup - so the row/column meaning is inferred from the layout caller, not from the code.

name: maybe_Text_Layout_SetLineLimit
signature: void maybe_Text_Layout_SetLineLimit(uint8_t* lineCounter, TextLayout* layout, uint32_t limit)
summary: Stores the line budget at layout+0x4C and returns immediately when the current line counter already reached it or exceeds 3; otherwise it continues building the next line record (the tail constructor is marked noreturn by the decompiler).
evidence: The caller Text_LayoutSingleLine and the counter/limit compares match the disassembly; the truncated tail means the function does more than the name says, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate
signature: void maybe_Math_Vector3_Interpolate(float* unused, float* from, float* out, uint32_t mode)
summary: Small adapter used by the 'interpolate owner vector' helpers: it builds a 3-word record from its third argument (0x0039CD08) and forwards it with the second argument and the mode word to 0x0039CBBC; the first argument is never read here.
evidence: The five callers (Battle_Unit_ApplyModelParts and four maybe_Field_InterpolateOwnerVector* helpers) all pass (manager, from, outVector, mode) and the disassembly shows r0 is overwritten before use; the actual interpolation lives in 0x0039CBBC (currently named Text_LayoutSingleLine, an implausible name for this context), so the wrapper's own name stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_RecordDetailWindow_HandleInputE
summary: Window input handler: pops the sub-pane on event bit 4, forwards the event position to the widget at +0xB4, and on event bit 0x102 pushes one of three sub-panes (+0x168/+0x1D0/+0x238) according to the row-type byte at self->f_EC->f_C, each with its own text index and descriptor pair from 0x0072A284.
evidence: The three-way sub-pane push and the descriptor table are clear; 'RecordDetailWindow' and the 'E' suffix are still inherited from the first pass - no caller exists and the row-type field is unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_CreateItemModelFromRecord
summary: Applies one input event to a window: pops the sub-pane when the event's cancel bit is set and then creates/attaches the item model at self+0x30 from the event's three geometry fields (+0x16/+0x17/+0x18).
evidence: The item-model callee is now named (maybe_Ui_ItemModel_CreateAttached), which supports 'CreateItemModel', but it is itself below 0.5 and the window class is unnamed, so this stays maybe_.

name: Shop_GoldWouldExceedCap
signature: u32 Shop_GoldWouldExceedCap(u32 unusedA, u32 itemId, int count)
summary: Returns 1 when buying `count` of an item would push the party's gold past the 9,999,999 cap: looks the item row up, multiplies its price-like field (+0x1C) by count, adds the gold at bag+0x28 (work+0x24AC0) and compares with 0x0098967F. The first argument is not read (the lookup id arrives in r1).
evidence: The constant 0x0098967F and the read at work+0x24A98+0x28 = work+0x24AC0 are the gold cap and the gold word from FACTS.md, and the named caller Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry uses the result to refuse a purchase; the disassembly confirms Item_LookupRecord(dst=r1 id) followed by price*count+gold.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_Restore
signature: void maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_Restore(UiShopItemList* shop, int screen, int arg3, int context)
summary: Shop item-list step handler: if the page scroll is finished it chains to Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry with the context flags cleared; otherwise it writes screen command 0x1E, reactivates the screen and returns the default handler pair from 0x007295C0. Its twin 0x001E93E0 is identical except for command 0x1F and the 0x10100 confirm flag.
evidence: Only the command id (0x1E vs 0x1F) and the context flag differ between the two twins, and nothing in the body names the step; 'Restore' is therefore still an unverified label.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_Open
signature: void maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_Open(UiShopItemList* shop, int screen, int arg3, int context)
summary: Shop item-list step handler: when the page scroll is finished it chains to Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry with the confirm flag 0x10100 set; otherwise it writes screen command 0x1F, reactivates the screen and returns the default handler pair from 0x007295C0.
evidence: The 0x10100 flag is the positive/confirm marker of this family, but the 0x1F command id has no name and the twin 0x001E935C does the mirror step, so 'Open' remains a first-pass reading.

name: Ui_ItemScreen_SetSelectedItem
summary: Records the selected item id in the screen byte at +0x49 and re-renders the item-name line: formats the name through the std::wstring formatter (0x006F0E5C) and writes it into the text pane selected by the screen's +0x28 field.
evidence: Three named confirm handlers (Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput, Ui_ItemScreen_ConfirmEntryEx, Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry) call it, and the disassembly shows the wstring format (0x006F0E5C) followed by the pane text setter 0x001A6680 with the pane index from +0x28 and the id stored at +0x49 - the 'current selection' reading is now supported.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_SelectQuantity
summary: Quantity spinner handler of the shop item list: forwards the event to the spin control at screen+0x1E08 (vtable +0x3C), stores the control's current quantity in shop[5], shows price*quantity in the number pane via Ui_SetNumberTextPane1, and on the confirm event (0x102) calls Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry; on cancel it returns the default pair from 0x007295C0.
evidence: The body reads the quantity from the spin control and multiplies the looked-up item price by it before writing the number pane - exactly a quantity-selection step - and all five callees are now named shop/UI helpers.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DetachChildEx
summary: Variant of the detach pair for the shop list pane at self+0x244C: refreshes the pane (0x001EA614), re-links the owner (0x00123594) and broadcasts message 0 to the pane's children.
evidence: Same body as 0x001EAAA0/0x001EAC04 with a different node offset, and the only caller is the unproven maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry; the verb stays generic.

name: Sound_StopHandleWithFade
signature: u32 Sound_StopHandleWithFade(SoundSystem* self, u32 handle, float fade)
summary: Stops a sound by handle: masks the handle with the system's enable byte, scans the 0x40-entry handle table at +0x1848 and, on a match, clears the entry and releases it; if the BGM state byte at +0x1A50 is 6 it moves it to 7 and fades the channel from +0x44 to the given gain through Snd_FadeChannelToGain.
evidence: Callers are StopME and three Ui_JockeyPanel fade/teardown steps (so both BGM and minigame channels), and the body's handle-table walk plus the Snd_FadeChannelToGain call are explicit; 'StopHandleWithFade' no longer claims BGM-only.

name: maybe_Ui_CasinoWindow_CtorLiteralPool
summary: Not code: 0x0024039C and 0x002403A0 are the two literal-pool words (0x0076B520, 0x0076B1D8) that the constructor ending at 0x00240384 loads; the first real function after them starts at 0x002403A4 (a deleting destructor). Named only so the address is covered.
evidence: Disassembly confirms the pool: 0x00240384 is pop {r4,r5,r6,pc}, the two words follow, and 0x002403A4 begins push {r4,lr}; bl 0x002403B4; pop; b 0x0010F6CC. The readable C shown for this address is the neighbour's body, not code at 0x0024039C. Whether the pool belongs to the CasinoWindow constructor is still unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_DebugMenu_UpdateState
summary: Page-sequence state machine (states 0-4 in self+0x11): waits for the page to become ready, runs the frame-delta check, waits for the animation to finish and then accumulates frame time until 1.8 s (0x3ECCCCCD) before advancing the page; always returns 1.
evidence: The callees are named UI transition/animation helpers unrelated to debugging and nothing in the body reads a debug flag - 'DebugMenu' is inherited from the unproven name of the adjacent 0x003EB174; the page/attract reading cannot be confirmed without the owner of vtable 0x00782950.

name: maybe_Ui_AdvanceChildWhenIdle
summary: Vtable step of a small window: when the UI input manager's slot +0x38 is empty (no active input receiver) it asks the child at self+8 to switch to state 3 through its virtual +0x14; always returns 1.
evidence: Same four-line body as 0x0029954C and 0x004A66D0 with a different input-manager slot (+0x38 / +0x3C+0x40 / +0x34); the slots are unnamed, so 'AdvanceChildWhenIdle' remains a description of the call pattern.

name: maybe_Ui_AdvanceChildWhenIdleB
summary: Second copy of the 'advance the child to state 3 when the input manager is free' vtable step: here both input-manager slots +0x3C and +0x40 must be empty before the child's virtual +0x14 is called with 3.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x00249448 apart from testing two input-manager slots instead of +0x38; the shared behaviour is clear but the slot names are unknown, so the 'B' twin label stays and the name remains maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_AdvanceChildWhenIdleC
signature: int maybe_Ui_AdvanceChildWhenIdleC(UiWidget* self, int arg2, int b, int c)
summary: Third copy of the 'advance the child to state 3 when the input manager is free' vtable step, testing the input-manager slot +0x34; returns 1 so the caller treats the frame as handled.
evidence: Same two-call body as 0x00249448/0x0029954C with the third input slot (+0x34); no caller and no named slot, so the previous 'HandleConfirm' reading (which implied confirm-button handling) stays replaced by the honest 'advance child when idle' at low confidence.

name: Gfx_BillboardObjectCtorBase
summary: Shared base constructor for billboard-style gfx objects: runs the descriptor constructor Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4 (with the hidden stack argument) and installs the billboard object vtable plus the default word/zero fields at +0x2C..+0x38; the derived constructors overwrite the vtable afterwards.
evidence: The body installs maybe_g_gfxBillboardObjectVtable right after Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4, which identifies the base class as a billboard object rather than an 'animation object'; the four callers (Field_EnemyAiAnimCtor/B and two enemy-AI anim factories) are derived constructors that replace the vtable.

name: Actor_ActionTable_Ctor
signature: void Actor_ActionTable_Ctor(void* self, Actor* actor, void* def, char* name, int flags)
summary: Constructor of the per-actor action table: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor with the caller's stack argument, zeroes the bookkeeping words +0x2C..+0x84 and default-constructs 0x39 (57) entries of 0x30 bytes with the action ctor 0x004A55B0; the single caller Actor_CreateActionTable creates one per actor from the action-set name.
evidence: The only caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable and the disassembly shows the 0x39 x 0x30 std_ConstructArray of the action ctor - the 'action table' reading is supported; the installed vtable symbol (maybe_g_eventGimmickVtable) is still unexplained but does not change the table role.

name: Actor_Action_CreateCurveMove
summary: Creates a curve-move action entry (opcode 2): allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs g_actorActionCurveMoveVtable, copies the two default control-point words from 0x007BE2D4, clears the three state words and builds the embedded cubic curve at +0x13 with 0x0017C4CC.
evidence: The installed vtable is the project's named g_actorActionCurveMoveVtable (0x0075FC60), the caller is Actor_CreateActionTable and the disassembly shows the opcode 2 write - the class is no longer a guess.

name: Actor_Action_CreateCurveMove2
summary: Creates the second curve-move action variant (opcode 4): installs g_actorActionCurveMove2Vtable, copies the same default control-point words, stores the extra callback 0x002BF5B0 at +0x4C and builds the embedded curve at +0x14.
evidence: The vtable is g_actorActionCurveMove2Vtable and the opcode field is 4, so the first-pass 'Jump2' name claimed a jump the code does not show; the caller is Actor_CreateActionTable.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_CreateStateAction
summary: Action-table entry constructor: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x00762850, copies the two default words from 0x007BE2D4 and 0x007AE734 and sets the two state ids 1 and 2 at +0xD/+0x10.
evidence: The caller Actor_CreateActionTable proves it is an action-class constructor, not a field actor state; 'InitCarry' and 'Field_ActionState' both asserted meanings the body does not have, so the name is corrected to the honest 'CreateStateAction' and stays maybe_ because the two ids are unnamed.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_CtorSimpleB
summary: Small action-table entry constructor: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x0076592C and copies the two default words from 0x007BE2D4.
evidence: The caller is Actor_CreateActionTable and the installed vtable is a per-entry action class, so 'Field_Actor' was the wrong family; the class-specific behaviour is a single vtable word, so it stays maybe_.

name: FlwAction_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the flw action entry: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor with the caller's stack argument and installs g_flwActionVtable; nothing else is initialised.
